notes: Ancient Beast is a client-only Vite + Phaser 4 turn-based strategy game, so it is served as a static production build (bun 1.4.2 per packageManager, node 24 pinned in mise.toml; deps installed with `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, and the native `canvas` test dependency was given its prebuilt binary by hand). Rebuild with `.ui-capture/build.sh`, which runs `bun run build` and copies deploy/ (minus source maps) to .ui-capture/out. DATA: the 'established user' state is a match in progress. seed/record-match.test.ts plays a real match with the repo's own headless bot harness (src/__tests__/simulation/botgeria, run via `node_modules/.bin/jest --config .ui-capture/jest.record.config.js record-match`) using a veteran's settings: 1v1, seat 1 human vs bot, 60 plasma, 4 active units, unit drops on, ability upgrades after 3 uses, Dragon Bones arena. It records the game's own GameLog (154 actions: summons, moves, abilities, skips) and cuts it at the start of the player's Swampler turn in round 8. seed/match.ab is passed at build time as DEBUG_GAME_LOG, the game's built-in way to load a log on startup (DEBUG_MODE=true, the repo default). On open, the pre-match screen shows briefly, then the match loads and replays. replay-fastforward.js (a capture helper injected into out/index.html) presses the game's own replay Fast Forward control once, so within roughly 10-30 s the board shows the round-8 position: both Dark Priests plus about 8 summoned units (Knightmare, Headless, Impaler, Swampler, Nutcase vs Impaler, Swampler, Bounty Hunter), with partial health, plasma spent, queue, combat log and the player's turn active. seed/replay-match.test.ts checks headlessly that the log replays with 0 dropped actions. MAIN AREAS: the hex battlefield with creature queue (top), active unit portrait and abilities (left), turn/flee/delay/skip/audio controls and combat log; the dashboard/creature roster (hotkey D or the Godlet Printer button) with unit cards, stats and the Open Collective supporter marquee; the scoreboard (hotkey Tab); the music player; the pre-match setup screen (players, plasma, active units, timers) appears briefly on load and again after leaving the match. Headless Chromium could not run inside the sandbox, so the final rendering was not checked in a real browser; the served files, stub endpoints and SPA fallback were checked over HTTP.
